answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent network can mandate sequential delay functions verified by a cryptographic kernel. Nodes compute non-parallelizable iterations each epoch to prove elapsed time. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of dedicating scarce processor time per identity, preventing one machine from spawning hollow peers. However, consensus timing fragments like brittle shale under network jitter, and custom ASICs grant wealthy operators an unfair speed advantage.
